title: As-Salam, the Source of Peace
hookLine: the Source of Peace, and why the greeting goes to those you know and those you don't
tomorrow: peace on the outside. but what makes a heart feel safe?

lines: PEACE IS A NAME OF ALLAH.
cards: A greeting is usually just noise. As-salamu alaykum isn't: it means peace be upon you, and Peace, As-Salam, is a name of Allah. Pickthall's list in Surah al-Hashr runs: the Holy One, Peace.
Then the strange detail. Someone asked the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, what in Islam is best.
Bukhari records his answer, in paraphrase: feed people, and give the greeting of peace to those you know and those you don't. Why strangers? Why not just your own people?

teach.b: Here's the solve. A greeting to people you know keeps a circle warm.
A greeting to people you don't makes the circle bigger. And the Qur'an draws that circle as wide as it goes. In Surah al-Hujurat, Pickthall has: O mankind!
We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Not so you'd stay apart; so you'd know one another.
One human family, many tribes, and a greeting is the first step of the knowing.
Peace even goes to the rude: the Qur'an describes the servants of the Beneficent as people who, when the foolish speak to them, answer: peace.
So why use a name of God for hello?

Scholars have read the greeting two ways at once: may the peace of Allah be on you, and may As-Salam, who is Peace, be with you. Either way, you're handing someone you've never met the safest thing you have.
Something to tell a friend tonight: the answer to 'what in Islam is best?' included saying hello to strangers.

how: Muslims greet one another with as-salamu alaykum and answer wa alaykum as-salam, and every prayer ends with the same greeting of peace.

Surah al-Hujurat, in Pickthall: that ye may know one another.

games.q: a new kid sits alone at lunch every day. you don't know him, and your friends say he's 'not really one of us.' what fits the hadith on greeting?
o: greet him; peace is for the people you know and the ones you don't.
wait until he says hi first; greeting strangers can come off weird.
greet only your own circle first; that's where peace has to start.
games.why: feed people and greet those you know and those you don't: the greeting is how the circle gets bigger.

practice: Say it out loud, softly, three times, the way you'd say it to a face: as-salamu alaykum, peace be upon you. Each time, bring a different person to mind: someone you love, someone you barely know, someone you find hard.
For the sit, stay with the last one.

wordCard.voice: As-Salam: the Source of Peace, a name of Allah folded into every as-salamu alaykum.

orig.note: Arabic: peace, safety, wholeness; As-Salam, the Source of Peace, is a name of Allah.

carryVoice: Keep this one: peace, for the people I know and the people I don't. Until next time.
